post.summary:
* POST /api/v0/exercise-services/client/exercises/:id/files
 *
 * Stores files for a later submission to this exercise. Every multipart field name must be a
 * UUID the client picks; the host assigns the ids a submit request then names. Uploads are
 * bound to this exercise and user, and unreferenced ones are reaped, so a client should upload
 * immediately before submitting.
 *
 * Gated on the caller being able to answer the exercise at all, so stored objects cannot be
 * accumulated past a deadline or a closed exam. The per-slide try limit is only checked across the
 * whole exercise here, because this route is bound to an exercise rather than a slide. Files for a
 * snapshot (`?for=snapshot`) skip the deadline, try-limit and chapter-lock checks, as the
 * snapshot route does.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Exercise id

parameters.name: for
parameters.description: `snapshot` for files a `snapshots` request will name; absent means a submission's.

schema.description: What the uploaded files will be named in.

parameters.name: X-Client-Version
parameters.description: Optional client version; obsolete clients get 426

requestBody.description: One file part per file, each field name a distinct client-chosen UUID and each part carrying a file name

200.description: The stored files, in the order the parts were sent

401.description: The bearer token is missing or was rejected

403.description: The token lacks the `exercise-services` scope (message_key `insufficient_scope`), the user may not view this exercise (`no_access`), its chapter has not opened yet (`chapter_not_open_yet`), chapter locking keeps it closed (`chapter_not_unlocked_yet`, `chapter_completed_and_locked`), or the exercise is locked for the user (`exercise_locked`); neither lock is checked for `?for=snapshot`

404.description: No exercise with the given id exists

422.description: The user is not enrolled to this exercise's course, or for `?for=snapshot` never was (message_key `not_enrolled`), the exercise can no longer be answered because its deadline has passed (`deadline_passed`) or every slide is out of tries (`out_of_tries`) (neither checked for `?for=snapshot`), or the multipart body violates the field-name, file-count or size rules

426.description: The client is obsolete and must be upgraded

429.description: The user has uploaded too many files recently (message_key `rate_limited`)

post.summary:
* POST /api/v0/exercise-services/client/exercises/:id/snapshots
 *
 * Stores an ungraded copy of an answer: a paste to share, or a backup kept before local changes are
 * discarded. A snapshot uses no try, awards no points and is never graded, so it is accepted after
 * the deadline and when out of tries. Its files come from this exercise's `files` endpoint,
 * uploaded with `?for=snapshot`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Exercise id

parameters.name: X-Client-Version
parameters.description: Optional client version; obsolete clients get 426

requestBody.description: Why the snapshot is stored, the slide and task it is for, and the files it consists of

401.description: The bearer token is missing or was rejected

403.description: The token lacks the `exercise-services` scope (message_key `insufficient_scope`), the user may not view this exercise (`no_access`), or its chapter has not opened yet (`chapter_not_open_yet`)

404.description: No exercise with the given id exists, the exercise belongs to an exam, or the referenced slide/task does not exist

422.description: The user never enrolled on this exercise's course (message_key `not_enrolled`), the referenced slide/task belongs to another exercise, the task's exercise service cannot be served to this client, no files are named, or a named upload was reaped (`upload_expired`), was never uploaded for this exercise by this user (`unknown_upload`) or was named more than once (`duplicate_upload`)

426.description: The client is obsolete and must be upgraded

429.description: Too many pastes of this exercise by this user recently

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Exercise id

parameters.name: X-Client-Version
parameters.description: Optional client version; obsolete clients get 426

requestBody.description: The slide and task being answered, and the answer: its JSON, the ids of the files it consists of, or both

200.description: The created submission, identified by both its task and slide submission ids

401.description: The bearer token is missing or was rejected

403.description: The token lacks the `exercise-services` scope (message_key `insufficient_scope`), the user may not view this exercise (`no_access`), its chapter has not opened yet (`chapter_not_open_yet`), chapter locking keeps it closed (`chapter_not_unlocked_yet`, `chapter_completed_and_locked`), or the exercise is locked for the user (`exercise_locked`, see `ExerciseProgress.exercise_locked`)

422.description: The user is not enrolled to this exercise's course (message_key `not_enrolled`), its deadline has passed (`deadline_passed`), the slide is out of tries (`out_of_tries`), the referenced slide/task belongs to another exercise, the task's exercise service or another task's on the slide cannot be served to this client, a `file` answer names no files or a `json` one names files, or a named upload was reaped (`upload_expired`), was never uploaded for this exercise by this user (`unknown_upload`) or was named more than once (`duplicate_upload`)

AnswerFile.description:
A file the host stored on a client's behalf. The host assigns `id`; a client never invents
one. Returned by the upload endpoint and echoed back by submission download.

id.description: The host's file id. Names this file in a submit request.

name.description: The original file name the client sent.

order_number.description:
The file's position in the answer it belongs to. `None` for a file that is not part of an
answer yet, which is every file the upload endpoint returns.

size_bytes.description:
`None` for a file stored before the size was recorded; never a substitute zero, so a client
can tell an unknown size from an empty file.

url.description: Direct download URL; needs no bearer token.

AnswerKind.description:
Which of the two representations an answer is: the JSON in `data_json`, or the files in
`data_files`. A request that omits it means `Json`.

AnswerSnapshotResult.description:
Result of storing a snapshot. `snapshot_id` is what `submissions/{id}/download` (and, for a
paste, `submissions/{id}/share`) takes, and what the submissions list reports as the entry's `id`.

ApiErrorResponse.description: Canonical API error envelope returned for controlled application errors.

ChapterLockingStatus.description:
Where the user is in a course's chapter locking, which opens chapters one at a time as the
previous ones are completed.

ClosedChapter.description: A chapter of the course that opens later.

chapter_number.description: The chapter's position in the course, from 1.

Course.description: A course the current user is enrolled on or teaches.

ai_policy.description:
The teacher's AI-use policy for the course, uninterpreted: what each value permits is the
client's decision. Absent from a host that predates the field, which reads as `not_set`.

closed_at.description:
When the course run ended or ends; the course takes no new students from then on. Absent
for a course with no end, and from a host that predates the field.

is_enrolled.description:
Whether the user has a live enrollment on the course. A course the user only teaches is
listed without one, and submits to it are refused with `not_enrolled`. Absent from a host
that predates the field.

is_staff.description:
Whether the user teaches or assists on the course. Staff are served exercises of chapters
that have not opened yet, and model solutions whatever their own progress.

language_code.description:
The course's language as an IETF BCP 47 tag, e.g. `en-US` or `fi-FI`. Absent from a host
that predates the field.

language_group_id.description:
Shared by every language version of the course; versions are different courses with
different exercises. Absent from a host that predates the field.

moved_to_course_id.description:
The language version of this course the user now studies, when they have moved from this
course to another version. Absent otherwise, and from a host that predates the field.

organization_name.description: Denormalized so a client needn't resolve the owning organization separately.

successor_course_id.description: The course that continues this one after it ended, if its teacher named one.

url.description: The course material's front page. Absent from a host that predates the field.

CourseAiPolicy.description: A course's AI-use policy as chosen by its teacher.

CourseProgress.description:
The current user's progress across the course exercises this client is served, returned
by `courses/{id}/progress` in a single round-trip. Course-level totals are not sent
separately; the client derives them by summing over `exercises` (e.g. total awarded =
`sum(score_given)`, total available = `sum(score_maximum)`).

closed_chapters.description:
The chapters that have not opened yet, with the user's progress on the exercises that
`courses/{id}/exercises` will list once the chapter opens; a chapter with none is left out.
Those exercises are absent from `exercises` and from `courses/{id}/exercises` until the
chapter opens, so a client must not take their absence to mean they were removed. Absent
from a host that predates the field.

course_id.description: The course these progress entries belong to; echoes the path id.

exercises.description: The user's progress on the open chapters' exercises that `courses/{id}/exercises` lists.

CurrentUser.description: The user the bearer token acts for, so a client can tell when a login switched accounts.

email.description: Absent from a host that predates the field.

id.description: Stable for the lifetime of the account.

name.description:
The account's name as the user entered it, for showing which account is logged in. Absent
when the user has not given one, and from a host that predates the field.

Exam.description:
An exam the user has started and can still answer. Its exercises come from `exams/{id}/exercises`;
their gradings stay hidden until the user can no longer answer the exam.

answerable_until.description:
The user's answers are accepted until this moment: the end of their time or of the exam,
whichever comes first.

started_at.description: When the user started the exam.

ExerciseChapter.description:
The chapter an exercise belongs to, for grouping a course's exercises the way its material
does.

chapter_number.description: The chapter's position in the course, from 1.

oneOf.description:
The user's status in the course's chapter locking. Submissions to the chapter's exercises
are refused unless it is `unlocked`. Absent when the course does not lock chapters, and from
a host that predates the field.

ExerciseProgress.description:
The current user's progress on a single exercise.

`standing` is the client's passed/failed signal. `completed` is the activity stage, which
an exercise without peer or self review reaches on any graded submission, even one
worth 0 points.

attempted.description:
`true` once the user has started or submitted the exercise (any activity stage past
the initial one), regardless of whether it is completed.

completed.description: `true` once the exercise has reached the `Completed` activity stage.

exercise_locked.description:
`true` once the exercise takes no more submissions from the user, whatever the chapter's
`locking_status` says: their answer was locked for review, graded by a teacher, or locked
unanswered with its chapter. Only a teacher resetting the exercise lifts it. Submits are
refused with 403 `chapter_completed_and_locked` while the chapter is locked for the user,
and with `exercise_locked` otherwise. Absent from a host that predates the field.

max_tries.description:
How many graded submissions the exercise accepts per slide. Absent when tries are
unlimited, and from a host that predates the field.

oneOf.description:
What the user's points wait for while a teacher review holds them back; `score_given` is
`0.0` until then. Absent when no points are held back, including when the answer got its
points before the course turned chapter locking on, and from a host that predates the field.

Where the user's answer is in the exercise's review process, which runs in the course
material. Absent while the user can still answer, and from a host that predates the field.

score_given.description: Points the user has been awarded, `0.0` when the user has no state for the exercise.

score_maximum.description: The maximum points obtainable from the exercise.

oneOf.description: Absent only from a host that predates the field.

A teacher's grading of the user's answer, which overrides the automatic score. Absent when
no teacher has graded the current answer, when the teacher awarded full points or hid the
grading, and from a host that predates the field.

tries_left.description:
How many of `max_tries` are left on the slide the user answers. Absent when tries are
unlimited, and from a host that predates the field.

ExerciseSlide.description:
One selected slide of an exercise, carrying only the tasks whose exercise service can serve
the requesting client. An exercise with no client-servable task, or whose slide also has tasks
the client cannot answer, is omitted entirely by endpoints that return this type, rather than
appearing with an empty `tasks`.

oneOf.description: Absent for an exercise outside any chapter, and from a host that predates the field.

course_id.description:
The course the exercise belongs to, so a client need not resolve it separately. The nil
UUID for an exam exercise, which `exam_id` names instead.

deadline.description:
The effective deadline: the exercise's own, else its chapter's. Submissions are refused
from this moment on.

exam_id.description:
The exam the exercise belongs to; absent for a course exercise, and from a host that
predates the field.

exercise_order_number.description:
The exercise's position on its page, from 0. Positions repeat across pages; the course's
exercise list is already in material order.

page_url.description:
The course material page the exercise is on, where the student can also see their latest
submission and its grading. Absent from a host that predates the field.

ExerciseSlideSubmission.description:
Body of `POST exercises/{id}/submit`. Plain JSON — no file parts, no archive: the previously
uploaded files named here are the answer.

oneOf.description: Absent means `json`. A client answering with files sends `file`.

data_files.description:
Ids from this exercise's `files` endpoint, in the order they are to be graded and
displayed. A `file` answer must name at least one, and every id must have been uploaded by
this user for this exercise.

data_json.description:
The exercise service's own JSON: the whole answer for a `json` answer, the service's
metadata about the files for a `file` one.

ExerciseSlideSubmissionListItem.description:
A past submission or snapshot of the current user to an exercise. `id` is what
`submissions/{id}/download` takes, and `submissions/{id}/share` for anything but a backup.

is_shared.description:
Whether the entry has a live share link right now, whatever its kind: a paste can have been
revoked, and a graded submission can have been shared from elsewhere.

kind.description: Absent from a host that predates the field, which lists only submissions.

ExerciseStanding.description: Where the user stands on an exercise, decided by the host so every client agrees.

ExerciseTask.description:
One task of an exercise slide, as produced by a specific exercise service.

`public_spec` / `model_solution_spec` are plugin-owned blobs: the exercise service
that produces them is the only component that interprets their shape, so the host
forwards them verbatim and they stay opaque `serde_json::Value` here.

ExerciseTaskSubmissionResult.description:
Result of a submit. Carries both ids so a client never re-derives one from the other:
grading polling takes `task_submission_id`, download/share take `slide_submission_id`.

oneOf.description:
The user's progress on the whole exercise as of this poll, so a client can record
completion without a separate `courses/{id}/progress` round-trip. Absent for an exam
exercise, and from a host that predates the field.

feedback_json.description:
Structured grading feedback, opaque like `ExerciseTask`'s spec fields: only the
exercise service that produced it interprets its shape.

feedback_text.description: Human-readable feedback, for a client to display as-is.

score_given.description:
What the grading gave this submission. Absent until grading has produced a value; a
partial value while `grading_progress` is still pending. The exercise's awarded points
need not include it while a teacher review is pending (see `exercise_progress`).

submission_page_url.description:
The course material page of the exercise, anchored at the exercise, where the user's
latest submission and its grading are shown. Absent for an exam exercise, and from a
host that predates the field.

oneOf.description:
The submission belongs to an exam the user can still answer, which keeps its grading
hidden until then, or to a manually graded exam, whose results are the teacher's decisions.

ExerciseTaskSubmissionStatus.description: The grading status of a task submission, as polled after `submit`.

GradingProgress.description: How far along a task submission's grading is.

NewAnswerSnapshot.description:
Body of `POST exercises/{id}/snapshots`. Names files from this exercise's `files` endpoint
like a `file` submit does, uploaded with `?for=snapshot` so that a passed deadline or used-up
tries do not refuse the upload.

data_files.description: At least one id, each uploaded by this user for this exercise.

data_json.description: The exercise service's own JSON about the files, as in a `file` submit.

PasteResult.description: A shareable URL for a submission or paste.

PendingTeacherReview.description:
What a user's points on an exercise wait for when a teacher reviews answers before awarding
points.

ReviewingStage.description:
Where an answer is in the review process of an exercise that uses peer, self or teacher review.
Every stage takes no new answers; the reviews themselves are done in the course material.

SnapshotPurpose.description:
Why a client stores an answer snapshot. Neither purpose is graded, uses a try or awards points,
and both are accepted after the deadline and when out of tries.

SubmissionFiles.description:
Response of `GET submissions/{id}/download`: the files the submission was made from, recovered
from the host's own file records rather than from the service's answer.

The same shape regardless of where the submission was made. A native client's uploads are
recorded as it names them; an answer made in the service's IFrame carries its files inside the
service's own answer, so the host asks the service to enumerate them and stores them the same
way. Empty only when the submission genuinely has no files — an exercise type with none, or a
service that declares no way to enumerate its answers' files.

SubmissionKind.description: What an entry in the submissions list is.

TeacherDecision.description: What a teacher decided about an answer.

TeacherReview.description: A teacher's grading of the user's answer to an exercise, as the course material shows it.

justification.description: The teacher's written reasoning, if they gave any.

score_given.description: The points the teacher awarded, replacing the automatic score.

UploadedFiles.description: Response of `POST exercises/{id}/files`, in the same order as the request's parts.

bearer_auth.description: Access token passed as an HTTP bearer token in the Authorization header.
